c2_split: With the committed comparator admission wall (llama 223.4 ms vs hipEngine 315.8 ms at C1, worklog 20260829T215206...-1921c9) and decode 23.6 vs 25.2 ms/token, the model predicts 1.504 s vs 1.355 s = 0.90x, which is the published deficit. Contribution: about 4.8% prefill fixed cost and 5.1% decode amortization. So half of C2 is task #12 and half is projection dispatch admission.

correction_2026-08-30_same_day.open_cause_instead: Why decode amortizes sub-linearly is again unexplained. The live hypothesis is that decode uses per-row GEMV kernels (_GGUF_PUBLIC_USE_GEMV_DECODE = True at qwen35_gguf.py:215, the same duplicated-route-boolean problem ledgered in docs/REFACTOR.md), so each wave row costs its own GEMV pass instead of sharing one weight read. That is measurable by flipping the decode literals the way prefill was flipped (2026-08-30-w7900-q4km-all-gemv-prefill-arm-rejected.json).

correction_2026-08-30_same_day.what_is_true: projection dispatch (decide_projection_dispatch, ProjectionDispatchCandidate) is wired only into hipengine/runtime/qwen35_paro_runner.py - it is not reachable from the GGUF path at all. For the GGUF AR path the field is computed in qwen35_gguf.py:9005 as bool(native_batch and native_decode_steps > 0), and native_batch=True is passed at exactly one site (:1877), inside the generate_detailed branch gated by plan.mode is GREEDY_FAST and len(prompts) > 1 and self.native_batch_decode. That branch is not the one the AR bench takes: an earlier branch routes GREEDY_FAST multi-prompt requests to _generate_ar_serving_slots when _gguf_ar_packed_decode_enabled() or _gguf_ar_stream_decode_enabled(), which is why every cell reports path gguf_packed_ar_server_decode. So false means "serving-slots decode was used, not the native_batch_decode continuous path" - both are c-aware native decode paths, and native_caware_decode was true in all 70 width>1 cells.
correction_2026-08-30_same_day.what_survives: The amortization measurement itself is arithmetic over published rate rows minus a separately measured prefill wall and does not depend on the flag: decode cost per token is 1.00x the weight-read ideal at C1, 1.52x at C2, 1.62x at C3, 2.69x at C8. The C2 split into roughly half prefill fixed cost and half decode amortization also survives, since it uses the comparator admission wall and the decode cost, not the flag.
correction_2026-08-30_same_day.what_was_wrong: mechanism_observed attributed the 80/80 throughput_claim_eligible=false to hipengine/dispatch/projection.py taking row_gemv_until_caware_benchmark for lack of a benchmark-accepted c-aware projection candidate. That attribution is false.

finding: Decode cost per token falls sub-linearly with width - 1.52x off the weight-bound ideal at C2, 1.62x at C3, 2.69x at C8 - i.e. weights are not amortised across rows. The scoreboard still wins from C3 up because llama.cpp is worse there; C2 is the width where that trade stops paying.
mechanism_observed: [SUPERSEDED - see correction_2026-08-30_same_day] throughput_claim_eligible is false in 80/80 AR cells of /tmp/he-c1c8-cap8, the packet behind the promoted AR row, while native_caware_decode is true in the 70 cells with width>1 and false in the ten C1 cells, which is the expected shape for a width-aware route. In hipengine/dispatch/projection.py that flag is only true on path benchmark_accepted_caware_projection; rows==1 takes row_gemv_c1 and rows>1 falls back to row_gemv_until_caware_benchmark when no benchmark-accepted c-aware projection candidate applies. The only accepted-evidence artifacts in the tree are July PARO safetensors runs (2026-07-09-...native-decode...-selected-full-rowchunks.json and siblings); nothing accepts a c-aware projection for the GGUF Q4_K_M path on gfx1100.
method: wall = width*24/rate from the published rows; per-token decode = (wall - F)/(width*24) with F = 295 ms, the measured median-of-3 wall of one ~42-token prefill. C1 landing at 1.00x the weight-read ideal (16 GB at ~460 GB/s) is a coincidence check on F, not a fit.
question: AR C2 is the one scoreboard deficit prefill cannot explain (0.90x at C2 while C3 is 1.47x). Where does it come from?
untested_inference: That admitting a c-aware projection candidate at rows>1 would move decode toward the weight-bound ideal. The bound on the prize is the ratio column above (1.52x-2.69x on decode time, less the non-projection share). Not measured: the candidates are supplied by the caller and were not exercised here.
what_this_does_not_say: The flag does not invalidate the published AR row: the walls are real and reproduce across independent runs to 0.13%. It says the engine did not use its fastest known projection route at width>1 because that route has no accepted benchmark for this model, so the row understates achievable decode rather than overstating it.
